transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (CTO, Lakeside), Sara Chen (Head of ML), Raj Patel (Infra)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan lee from redwood inference, i'm the AE on the account. uh priya's our solutions engineer, she'll walk through the model catalog and the optimize bits. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Michael: good, thanks. excited to see, we had a quick look at the landing page, curious about model selection for clinical summarization.
[00:12] Sara: yes, specifically we need a model that handles ~512 token notes, preserves PHI handling, and stays under our latency budget.
[00:20] Priya: great, that's exactly what the model catalog is designed for \u0014 filters for architecture, sequence length compatibility, quantization profiles, and verified benchmarks. i'll share my screen in a sec.
[00:28] Raj: quick infra note \u0014 we are considering both hosted API for quick rollout and a private VPC for compliance. we'll want BYOK and SOC2 proofs.
[00:36] Jordan: noted. we'll cover security slide later. ok priya over to you.

[02:05] Priya: all right so first slide \u0014 model catalog overview. you can search by task (summarization), by license (open models), and by perf profile. here's an example \u0014 two-community models, one is a 7b that we've benchmarked at ~120ms p95 on A100 for 256 tokens, and the other is an Llama2-13B variant that does better quality but is heavier.
[02:30] Michael: can you put numbers for 512 tokens? our typical note is ~400 tokens but we pad.
[02:36] Priya: sure, for 512 tokens the 7b quantized with 4-bit runs about 180-220ms p95 depending on batch and whether prefix KV cache is hit. the 13b runs ~280-350ms. those numbers are from our internal microbenchmarks \u0014 i'll send the spreadsheet. (link: /redwood/benchmarks/lakeside-demo)
[03:05] Sara: how much does quantization affect quality for clinical text? we can't hallucinate or drop entities.
[03:12] Priya: good question. we include a quality delta column in the catalog \u0014 small drop for well-calibrated 4-bit LLMs on summarization tasks, but we recommend running evals on your prompt sets. that's where Redwood Optimize helps: it suggests quantization + batch configs with predicted cost savings and an estimated quality delta.

[04:00] Jordan: and to be clear, Optimize can give recommendations like \"use 4-bit q4x on A100 for batch size 8, expect ~22% cost savings vs fp16\" \u0014 it's tied to model profiles.
[04:15] Raj: is there an easy compatibility matrix for hardware? like what works on T4, A10, A100, and the new H100?
[04:21] Priya: yes, the catalog exposes a matrix \u0014 columns are GPUs, rows are model variants (fp16, q4, q8), cells say supported + benchmarked or supported with caveats. note: some quantized kernels are optimized for Ampere/GA100 and require certain kernels; H100 has newer kernel paths so we sometimes see different perf. also, for H100 we have long-context optimizations.

[06:00] Michael: you mentioned KV cache earlier \u0014 can you explain how caching affects latency for repeated prompts?
[06:07] Priya: sure. if you have conversational prefixes or repeated instruction templates, prefix caching keeps token generation lower because the old context isn't re-evaluated. in our tests with prefix cache hit rates around 60%, p50 drops quite a bit; p95 less so but still measurable. we sometimes hear \"K-V cash\" in transcription \u0014 sorry, not cash, kv cache.
[06:30] (laughter)

[07:15] Sara: about compliance \u0014 can you confirm SOC 2 and BYOK for private? and what about audit logs retention?
[07:22] Jordan: yes, Red wood's hosted API is SOC 2 compliant; Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and full audit logs that can ship to your SIEM. we'll include our SOC 2 report and a diagram of the private control plane.
[07:40] Raj: good. also do you support SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC?
[07:45] Priya: yes, SAML SSO and RBAC are available across Dedicated and Private. Hosted has role tiers and integration options.

[09:00] Jordan: shifting back to selection \u0014 how do you want to prioritize quality vs latency vs cost?
[09:06] Michael: top priority is correctness and PHI protection, then latency. cost is secondary but important.
[09:12] Sara: we also want to limit hallucinations and make sure entity extraction for patient data is stable.

[10:00] Priya: ok we can set up an eval harness \u0014 you can upload prompt/eval sets and we'll run model comparisons across chosen candidates. the catalog will show per-model eval scores plus per-token cost estimates.
[10:20] Michael: is the eval run free? what's the turnaround?
[10:24] Priya: small runs are included as part of trial/pilot; larger runs can be in the pilot scope \u0014 typically 48-72 hours for a full sweep depending on dataset size.

[12:00] Priya: demo time \u0014 opening the console... here is the model detail for \"Redwood-Open-7B-q4\" \u0014 notes on license, architecture, tokenizer, max seq len, quantization flags, recommended GPU families. you can click \"compatibility matrix\" \u0014 see it lists A100 as benchmarked for q4 and T4 as experimental.
[12:30] Michael: can we filter models by license 'commercial'? we need to avoid copyleft for production.
[12:35] Priya: yes, filter by license is available; we'll prefilter for permissive commercial use.

[14:00] Jordan: let's talk throughput \u0014 what's expected tokens/sec for a 7b q4 on A100 for 512 tokens?
[14:07] Priya: ballpark 400-700 tokens/sec depending on batching; in production with batching and continuous batching across concurrent requests you can get higher amortized throughput. remember tradeoff \u0014 larger batches improve throughput but hurt tail latency.
[14:30] Raj: any routing/fallbacks if capacity is constrained? we may want multi-tier routing from hosted to dedicated.
[14:36] Priya: yes, smart routing policies can route by latency SLO, cost, region, or customer tier; can also fallback to smaller model variants if a node is saturated.

[16:00] Sara: about quality monitoring \u0014 how do we detect regressions after changing quantization or model version?
[16:07] Priya: Redwood Optimize links to eval prompt sets and continuous regression alerts \u0014 we can alert when quality metric drops beyond a threshold and auto-roll back to a previous model. the console also shows token-level cost impact.

[18:00] Michael: what's the typical pricing delta between hosted vs dedicated? we want rough numbers to compare ROI.
[18:08] Jordan: hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token and per-embedding rates; dedicated has reserved capacity with lower per-token costs but requires commit. i'll send an apples-to-apples sheet. for pilots we usually recommend hosted to iterate then move to dedicated for scale.

[20:00] Priya: another demo item \u0014 compatibility matrix exports as CSV so you can share with infra. here's an example row: model, variant, quant, gpu, p95(256), p95(512), notes. we'll attach that.

[22:30] Raj: for private deployments, what's the control plane architecture? do we need a separate on-prem agent?
[22:35] Jordan: Private uses a customer-managed control plane; there is an optional on-prem agent for air-gapped setups. in VPC mode, control plane is managed but network traffic stays in your VPC endpoints. we'll send the architecture diagram.

[25:00] Sara: any known issues with tokenizer mismatches across forks? we've seen tokenization differences cause scoring issues.
[25:07] Priya: we surface tokenizer and tokenizer hashes in the catalog; when model forks differ we flag that. also our eval harness normalizes tokenization where possible.

[28:00] Michael: ok, pilot \u0014 what would you need from us to start a benchmark?
[28:07] Priya: ideally a sample of 500-1,000 notes, target QPS, and success criteria (p95 latency threshold, accuracy measure). we'll run the sweep across 3 model variants and provide a CSV of results plus suggested config from Optimize.
[28:30] Raj: we can provide 1,000 anonymized notes and expected peak qps ~6 req/s, avg 2 req/s.
[28:35] Sara: accuracy metric is ROUGE + entity F1 on PHI redaction.

[30:00] Jordan: next steps quick recap \u0014 priya will share the benchmark spreadsheet and compatibility matrix; i'll send pricing and security docs; raj will share sample data and we'll schedule the pilot.
[30:12] Michael: sounds good. any blockers?
[30:15] Raj: only legal review on data transfer but we prefer VPC or private.
[30:20] Jordan: understood \u0014 we'll include our data flow diagram and SOC2.

[31:00] (brief cross talk; phones clatter)

[33:00] Priya: one more note on kernel selection \u0014 runtime picks kernels based on model shape and sequence length; sometimes for long-context we pick a different attention kernel which is faster on H100. i'll add notes to the matrix.

[35:00] Michael: what about monitoring \u0014 can we hook into Prometheus or do you push metrics?
[35:06] Priya: Dedicated and Private allow Prometheus endpoints; hosted can push to your cloud metrics or we can export via integrations.

[37:30] Jordan: okay wrapping up \u0014 we'll share the attachments: benchmark CSV, compatibility matrix, SOC2, architecture diagram, pricing sheet. any other questions?
[37:42] Sara: none from me. thanks.
[38:00] Michael: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[38:10] Raj: thanks everyone.
[41:00] Jordan: great, talk soon \u0014 we'll follow up with dates. bye.

(End of transcript - transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and filler)
